issues.legal_issue: The increased solatium does not apply to an award made before the retrospective period merely because an appeal concerning that award remains pending.
material_facts: The land was acquired under notifications issued well before the retrospective period for the amendment.
The claimant and the State appealed the compensation determination, and those appeals remained pending when the amendment was introduced.
The claimant sought the increased solatium on the ground that the compensation proceedings had not become final.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to the increased solatium because the award predated the retrospective period; the pendency of appeals did not bring the award within that period.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 23(2) and 30(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended by section 15(b) of the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984, make the increased solatium applicable to awards made during the specified retrospective period and to appellate orders arising from those awards. They do not extend it to older awards solely because an appeal is pending. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.original_award_predates_retroactive_peri: The original compensation award was made before the period to which the increased solatium applies retrospectively.
predicates.appeal_pending_during_transition: An appeal concerning the award remained pending during the transition associated with the amendment.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition compensation appeal concerns an award made before the retrospective period and remained pending during the transition, the increased solatium does not apply.
